institutionName: Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: To have the opportunity to live in a country where the culture is completely different from back home. I was certain that Rio would offer a great adventure.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very diffuclt to find information about the courses offered in english - they didnt offer them before having to apply for preaaprovals but it all worked out in the end. Besides that the webside provides a lot of information

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
PUC offers an intensive Portuguese course (1 month) before the semester starts, which you can sign up for (for an additional fee). I did it, and it was definitely worth it. During this course, you meet a smaller group of exchange students, have time to settle in before the semester begins, and also learn some of the language (which is a huge help).

Upon arrival – whether for the intensive course or at the start of the regular semester – there is an orientation day where you receive all the important information. I felt like I was in good hands and well supported by the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: There is a whole page on PUC´s webside to exchange studends which is very helpful. But info about the courses is more difficult.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
PUC doesn’t offer on-campus housing, but they do offer a “homestay program,” which I chose. Through this program, you can stay with a host family arranged by the university. It is not very expensive, and it is also possible for more than one student to stay together. I stayed with another girl from KU.

My host mom didn’t speak English, which made communication difficult at times, but it was also a good way to be forced to learn the language. It felt like a good and safe choice.

In the end, however, I moved out and found an Airbnb (which many of the other exchange students also did). A lot of students stayed in the homestay for a while and then moved out afterwards. This can feel a bit difficult, as you might feel some obligation toward the family you live with – but you are free to leave if you want to.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Airbnb is a good choice i would say. They also recommend a kollegie called U-living but this is a very expensive choice and when you sign the contract you obligate to stay the entire semester (at least to pay)

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted except one. My impression was that most exhange students got the courses they wanted but they might fill up and there is a quite stressful day where you quicly have to sign up for the classes you want - but you will get guidance in this.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: have some extra oppurtunies in case the courses you want is full.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wasent really academiclly challenged but it was also nice with a bit of a break, and many of courses offered in english is about Brasil. For example Brasilian culture or history - so it is a very nice way to get som information about the country you live in.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level isnt as hard as in Copenhagen but there is other challenges if you have courses in portuguese, which a lot of exhange students have. I also did even though i didnt speak any upon arrivel. But i could do the exams in english (which i first learned i could when i got there and talked to the teachers) but my impression was that a lot of the exhange students did the exams in english or passed anyways.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The english courses offered had a bit more creativity and also some fieldtrips etc. At PUC you have to attend to 75% of the classes to pass which is different from what i know from home. The expectations (academicly) is in general less than at KU i would say.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Brasilian culture, Inequality and diversity in urban context, portuguese language course and some courses at "ADM"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked Brasilian culture - here my exam was to do a documentary about a topic of my own choice and i also got some knowledge about the culture.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didnt really use any but there was some sport clubs offered.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: there is a club called "brother carioca" that arrange activites for and with the exhange students throughout the semester. PUC also offers some fieldtrips and social gatherings for exhange students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the intensive course!!! this was such a good way of meeting people and to settle before the regular semester.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to nearby cities like Sao paulo and Paraty but also just enjoy Rio. It is truly amazing with it beaches, hiking oppurtinies and the big national park located in the city. Be aware that travelling with airplane within Brasil is quite expensive and the distances is huge so be prepared to spend some time in buses:))

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took maybe a bit extra time because it is very different than here and also because of the language. It is a very big help to learn some portuguese before going. But the people there are so amazing and welcoming which helped so much with adapting. Also the city and culture is just amazing. I was a bit concered about the saftety before going and it is imoprtant to always take care when being there. It is not the same as being in Denmark and you should be more concered about which areas to be in, your belongings and walking+taking public transport late at night etc. But PUC also offers a lot of guidance for safety. And in general i felt very very safe. Rio is also a very touristy place.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: If you are up for the challenge then taking courses in portuguese is a good idea. But in general Brasilians are very welcoming and when you are out in the city or at campus people are very curious about you so i always felt like it was easy to socialize with locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe the safety concerns at first (but the longer i stayed the more safe i felt) and then the language - but this was also a fun challenge.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The people - their warmth and welcoming nature.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Do the intensive course 
2. Be prepared for a very busy and lively city - in the best way
3. Take your saftey concerns but dont let it stop you from going.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very helpful to learn some portuguese before going.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just living in the city. It has so much to offer. An amazing culture, the people and also the nature with mountains surrouding the city. There is always things to see and do.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Learning the language

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
